milestones.title: Shanghai becomes a market town
milestones.detail: The riverside village on the Huangpu was upgraded to a market town as the older port of Qinglong silted up. Some accounts instead date township status to 1267.
milestones.source: Danielson (2004), Shanghai and the Yangzi Delta, p. 9, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Shanghai#History

milestones.title: Shanghai County established
milestones.detail: Five townships were split from Huating to form Shanghai County under Songjiang Prefecture, with its seat at Shanghai Town, the later Old City.

milestones.title: City wall built against pirate raids
milestones.detail: A wall about 5 km round and 10 m high was raised around the county seat to resist wokou raids. Some sources give 1554.
milestones.source: Chen Boyi (2023), 防海之道：明代南直隶海防研究, and Perry, Shanghai on Strike, p. 15, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Old_City_(Shanghai)

milestones.title: Su-Song circuit intendant moves to Shanghai
milestones.detail: The regional intendant and the Jiangsu customs were now based in the town, which by mid-century had outgrown its walls towards the Huangpu wharves.
milestones.source: Johnson, Linda Cooke (1993), 'Shanghai: An Emerging Jiangnan Port, 1683-1840', in Cities of Jiangnan in Late Imperial China, via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Shanghai

milestones.title: Shanghai opens as a treaty port
milestones.detail: Opened to foreign trade by the 1842 Treaty of Nanking; the first British consul, George Balfour, was appointed in 1843.

milestones.title: British settlement laid out north of the walls
milestones.detail: The British concession was established outside the Chinese city, followed by American (1848) and French (1849) areas.

milestones.title: Small Swords Society seizes the walled city
milestones.detail: A Triad offshoot of the Taiping rebels occupied the Chinese city; refugees poured into the foreign settlements, which were left untouched.

milestones.title: International Settlement formed
milestones.detail: The British and American settlements merged into the Shanghai International Settlement, whose riverfront became the Bund.

milestones.title: Woosung railway, China's first, opens
milestones.detail: Jardine's built a line to Wusong; it was bought out by the Chinese authorities and dismantled in 1877.
milestones.source: Pong, David (1973), 'Confucian Patriotism and the Destruction of the Woosung Railway, 1877', Modern Asian Studies 7(4), via https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Shanghai

milestones.title: Old City walls dismantled
milestones.detail: The Ming walls were pulled down because they blocked the city's expansion.

milestones.title: Shanghai becomes a special municipality
milestones.detail: Shanghai was made a special city under the Nationalist government in 1927, and a municipality in May 1930.

milestones.title: Battle of Shanghai
milestones.detail: From 13 August to 26 November Chinese and Japanese forces fought for the city, which then fell under Japanese occupation.

milestones.title: People's Liberation Army takes Shanghai
milestones.detail: On 27 May 1949 the PLA took control of the city in the Shanghai Campaign.

milestones.title: Development of Pudong announced
milestones.detail: On 18 April 1990 Premier Li Peng announced the opening and development of Pudong, the district east of the Huangpu; Pudong New Area was established in 1992-93.

milestones.title: Shanghai Metro opens
milestones.detail: The first metro line began operating on 28 May 1993.

notes: Start date: the date Shanghai became a market town is contested. 1074 (Song dynasty) is the commonly quoted date and is used here as 'estimated'; another account dates township status to 1267. The securely documented step is the creation of Shanghai County in 1292. Neolithic sites (Majiabang/Songze culture, Qingpu) lie in the wider municipality, not on the city site, and are not used. Population: no figure was found before 1554. 1554-1900 follow Chandler (1987) as digitised by Reba et al. (2016), which describes the walled town and, after 1843, the town plus foreign settlements. Chandler's 1853 (225,000) and 1865 (146,232) values were left out: the 1865 figure appears to cover a narrower area than its neighbours. The 20th century is thin: the detailed municipal series (Zou Yiren 1980; Henriot's source book) could not be opened, so only Henriot's rounded totals for 1915 and 1948 are recorded; they cover the whole municipality and are not directly comparable with Chandler's 1900 figure (Chandler himself gives 1,000,000 for 1914 and 1,500,000 for 1925). Landmarks: skyscraper heights, years and positions are from the CTBUH Skyscraper Center; positions of older buildings are from OpenStreetMap (WGS-84) because some Wikipedia coordinates for Chinese sites are GCJ-02 shifted. The 977 date for Longhua Pagoda is for the brick core; the timber exterior has been renewed. Left out for lack of a sourced height: HSBC Building (1923), St. Ignatius Cathedral (1910), Jing'an Temple, City God Temple, Nanpu Bridge.
